entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
King Mu of Zhou, personal name Ji Man, was the fifth king of the Zhou dynasty of China. The dates of his reign are 976–922 BC or 956–918 BC.

He succeeded his father, King Jie, and ruled for approximately 54 years, implementing a series of reforms aimed at strengthening the Zhou state. Mu's policies focused on promoting agriculture, reducing military spending, and increasing infrastructure development.

One of his most notable achievements was the introduction of a new system of weights and measures, which helped standardize trade and commerce across the region. He also strengthened the Zhou army, modernizing its tactics and equipment to improve its effectiveness.

Mu's legacy extended beyond his own reign; he laid the groundwork for future Zhou rulers to build upon. His successor, King Kang, continued Mu's reforms and expanded the Zhou state's territories. The Zhou dynasty would go on to play a significant role in Chinese history for centuries to come.

Despite his many accomplishments, King Mu of Zhou is often remembered as a relatively obscure figure in Chinese historical records. However, his contributions to the development of the Zhou state cannot be overstated, and he remains an important figure in the study of ancient Chinese history.
